Roast notes, issue 14, November 2026

Two new coffees for the cold months

November brings the first lots of the Kenyan main crop and a Guatemala we have waited on since spring. Both go on the shelf on Tuesday 3 November, next to the two coffees most of you already drink.

New this month

Kenya Nyeri

Washed, from smallholders around Nyeri

Blackcurrant, pink grapefruit and brown sugar. Bright and juicy as filter.

£13.50 for 250 g

Shop Kenya Nyeri

New this month

Guatemala Huehuetenango

Washed, from the western highlands

Milk chocolate, red apple and almond. Easy as espresso or filter.

£11.00 for 250 g

Shop the Guatemala

Ridgeline Blend

Our house espresso, Brazil and Colombia

Cocoa, hazelnut and caramel. Holds its own in milk.

£9.50 for 250 g

Shop Ridgeline Blend

Colombia Decaf

Sugarcane process, from Huila

Panela, orange and a soft finish. A decaf that still tastes of coffee.

£10.50 for 250 g

Shop the decaf
 

On the bar: 1 to 16

We brew filter at 15 g of coffee to 240 g of water. For the Kenya, grind a touch finer than usual and aim to finish the pour at three minutes.

Read the brew guide

Saturday cupping, 14 November

Taste all four coffees side by side at the roastery from 10am. It is free and there is no need to book.

See the cupping details
